intro:
An indeterminate loading indicator.

[Button](/docs/components/button) renders one for you when `loading` is set, so a button does not need one passed in.

When you know how much is left, use [Progress](/docs/components/progress) instead.

examples.title: Inside a button
examples.description: You rarely need this — `Button`’s own `loading` prop inserts a variant-matched spinner for you.

examples.title: In another colour
examples.description:
`color` sets the turning arc and `trackColor` the faint ring behind it. Left unset they follow the theme's primary and muted colours.

Set them where the spinner sits on a surface the theme did not choose for it — a filled button, a photo, a coloured banner. There it wants the colour of the text around it, and the track wants to fade into the surface rather than read as a second spinner.
examples.code:
<Spinner color="#FFFFFF" />

// On a coloured surface, fade the track into it as well.
<View className="rounded-xl p-4" style={{ backgroundColor: brand }}>
  <Spinner color="#FFFFFF" trackColor="rgba(255,255,255,0.25)" />
</View>

examples.title: Naming the wait
examples.description: A spinner alone on a screen is the only thing announcing it, so give it words.
examples.code:
<View className="flex-1 items-center justify-center">
  <Spinner size="lg" label="Loading your dashboard" />
</View>

previewVideo.alt: The Spinner component, running in the example app.

notes:
A bare ring carries no words, so it is hidden from screen readers unless `label` is given. An unnamed progress indicator announces its role and nothing else, which is noise standing in for information.

Leave `label` off wherever something around the spinner already says the wait is on — `Button`'s `loading` state, a row with its own caption. Set it where the spinner is the only sign.

Under the platform's reduce-motion setting the ring stops turning and fades in place instead. It keeps moving because a spinner that holds still reads as one that has hung, which is the single thing a spinner exists to rule out.
